verses.sanskrit:
भीमसेन उवाच।
              सन्धिं कृत्वैव कालेन ह्यन्तकेन पतत्रिणा। अनन्तेनाप्रमेयेण स्त्रोतसा सर्वहारिणा॥१॥
verses.english: Bhima said : O great king, being mortal and unsubstantial as froth, unstable as fruit and dependant on time, how can you consider of any avail your having made an agreement in respect of Time, which is infinite and immeasurable, which passes as quickly as an arrow or a stream, carrying everything before it like death itself?

verses.sanskrit: प्रत्यक्षं मन्यसे कालं मर्त्यः सन्कालबन्धनः। फेनधर्मा महाराज फलधर्मा तथैव च॥२॥
verses.bhavadeepa: संधिमिति । पतत्रिणा बाणवत् शीघ्रगामिना प्राणहरेण वा । स्त्रोतसा नित्यवाहिना ॥१॥

verses.sanskrit: निमेषादपि कौन्तेय यस्यायुरपचीयते। सूच्येवाञ्जनचूर्णस्य किमिति प्रतिपालयेत्॥३॥
verses.english: O son of Kunti, how can he wait whose life is shortened every moment, as a quantity of collyrium is lessened each time, a grain is taken up by the needle?
verses.bhavadeepa: प्रत्यक्षं प्रत्यक्षेण ज्ञातम् । कालबन्धनः कालवश्यः फेनधर्मा निःसारः फलधर्मा पतनशीलः॥२॥

verses.sanskrit: यो नूनममितायुः स्यादथवापि प्रमाणवित्। स कालं वै प्रतीक्षेत सर्वप्रत्यक्षदर्शिवान्॥४॥
verses.english: Only he whose life has no limit or he who knows with certainty what the period of his life (really) is or he who knows the future as if it were placed before his eyes can wait for the arrival of (a certain fixed) time.
verses.bhavadeepa: सूच्येवाञ्जनचूर्णस्य यथा कज्जलक्षोदस्यातिश्लक्ष्णस्य सूक्ष्माग्रया सूच्यापि किंचिदपचीयते । एवं निमेषादपि यस्यायुरपचीयते स किमिति अवधिं प्रतिपालयेन्न कथमपीत्यध्याहृत्य योज्यम् । ‘चूर्णः क्षोदे क्षारभेदे’ इति विश्वः । शून्येवेति पाठेऽपि स एवार्थः । श्वयते प्रविशतीति शूनः स्थूलसूची ‘सूवा’ इति प्रसिद्धः । अल्पः शूनः शूनी तयेति योगात् । पूर्णस्येत्यपपाठः ॥३॥

verses.sanskrit: प्रतीक्ष्यमाणः कालो नः समा राजंस्त्रयोदश। आयुषोपचयं कृत्वा मरणायोपनेष्यति॥५॥
verses.english: O king, if we wait for thirteen years, that period of time will shorten our lives and bring us nearer to death.

verses.sanskrit: शरीरिणां हि मरणं शरीरे नित्यमाश्रितम्। प्रागेव मरणात्तस्माद्राज्यायैव घटामहे॥६॥
verses.english: Wealth is ever established in every creature having corporeal body. Therefore we should try to get possession of our kingdom before we meet with death.

verses.sanskrit: यो न याति प्रसङ्ख्यानमस्पष्टो भूमिवर्धनः। अयातयित्त्वा वैराणि सोऽवसीदति गौरिव॥७॥
verses.english: He who fails to achieve fame by not chastising his enemies is like a thing unclean. He is an useless burden of the earth as a brute is and perishes with ignominy.

verses.sanskrit: यो न यातयते वैरमल्पसत्त्वोद्यमः पुमान्। अफलं जन्म तस्याहं मन्ये दुर्जातजायिनः॥८॥
verses.english: The man, who being destitute of strength and courage, fails to chastise his enemies lives in vain. I consider such a man as low-born.
verses.bhavadeepa: याति प्राप्नोति । प्रसंख्यानं प्रकृष्टां साधुकीर्तिम्। यतः अस्पष्टः शौर्याद्यभावादितरैरविदितः भूमिवर्धनः भूमिहिंसकः । भूमेर्भारभूत इत्यर्थः अयातयित्वा अनिस्तीर्य । गौर्बलीवर्द इव । सोऽप्यशक्तश्चेत् गोषु संख्यानं स्पष्टतां वाप्यप्राप्नुवन्भूमेर्भारभूतो भवति ॥७॥

verses.sanskrit: हैरण्यौ भवतो बाहू श्रुतिर्भवति पार्थिवी। हत्वा द्विषन्तं सङ्ग्रामे भुङ्क्ष्व बाहुजितं वसु॥९॥
verses.english: Your hand can shower gold; your fame spreads over the whole earth. Therefore, killing your enemies in battle, enjoy the wealth acquired by the strength of your arms.

verses.sanskrit: हत्वा वै पुरुषो राजन्निकर्तारमरिन्दम। अह्नाय नरकं गच्छेत्स्वर्गेणास्य स संमितः॥१०॥
verses.english: O king, O chastiser of foes, if a man goes to hell on the very day he kills his injurer, that hell at once becomes heaven to him.
verses.bhavadeepa: हैरण्यौ हिरण्यस्वामिनौ । श्रुतिः कीर्तिः । पार्थिवी पृथोः राज्ञ इवेत्यर्थः ॥९॥

verses.sanskrit: अमर्षजो हि सन्तापः पावकाद्दीप्तिमत्तरः। येनाहमभिसन्तप्तो न नक्तं न दिवा शये॥११॥
verses.english: The pain that one feels in suppressing his anger is more burning than fire itself. I burn with it even now and I cannot sleep either in the night or in the day.
verses.bhavadeepa: निकर्तारं वञ्चकम् । अह्नाय सद्यः । स नरकम् आपदम् ॥१०॥

verses.sanskrit: अयं च पार्थो बीभत्सुर्वरिष्ठो ज्याविकर्षणे। आस्ते परमसन्तप्तो नूनं सिंह इवाशये॥१२॥
verses.english: This son of Pritha, Vivatsu (Arjuna) is foremost in drawing the bow-string. He is certainly much aggrieved, though he lives (quietly) like a lion in its den.

verses.sanskrit: योऽयमेकोऽभिमनुते सर्वान्ल्लोके धनुर्भृतः। सोऽयमात्मजमूष्माणं महाहस्तीव यच्छति॥१३॥
verses.english: This one (Arjuna) who desires to kill all the wielders of bow of the world without any body's) help, suppresses his wrath within his breast like a great elephant.

verses.sanskrit: नकुलः सहदेवश्च वृद्धा माता च वीरसूः। तवैव प्रियमिच्छन्त आसते जडमूकवत्॥१४॥
verses.english: Nakula, Sahadeva, the old mother of heroes (Kunti) are all sitting like dumb people in order to please you.
verses.bhavadeepa: अभिमनुते हिनस्ति । ‘यदि वेममभिमंस्ये कनीयोन्नं करिष्ये’ इति बृहदारण्यकादावभिपूर्वस्य मन्यतेर्हिंसार्थत्वदृष्टेः । इमं प्रथमजं सूक्ष्मं बीजभूतमिति श्रुतिपदस्यार्थः । आत्मजं चित्तजमूष्माणं तापम् ॥१३॥

verses.sanskrit: सर्वे ते प्रियमिच्छन्ति बान्धवाः सह सृञ्जयैः। अहमेकश्च सन्तप्तो माता च प्रतिविन्ध्यतः॥१५॥
verses.english: All our friends with the Srinjayas wish to , please you. Only I and the mother of Prativindhya, (Draupadi) are greatly aggrieved.

verses.sanskrit: प्रियमेव तु सर्वेषां यद्ब्रवीम्युत किञ्चन। सर्वे हि व्यसनं प्राप्ताः सर्वे युद्धाभिनन्दिनः॥१६॥
verses.english: And speak to you. Whatever I speak is (surely) agreeable to them all, for they plunged in great affliction eagerly wish for the battle.

verses.sanskrit: नातः पापीयसी काचिदापद्राजन्भविष्यति। यन्नो नीचैरल्पबलै राज्यमाच्छिद्य भुज्यते॥१७॥
verses.english: O king, what greater calamity would befall us than that our kingdom should be snatched away from us and enjoyed by weak and contemptible foes!

verses.sanskrit: शीलदोषाद्धृणाविष्ट आनृशंस्यात्परन्तप। क्लेशांस्तितिक्षसे राजन्नान्यः कश्चित्प्रशंसति॥१८॥
verses.english: O chastiser of foes, (only) from the weakness of your character you feel shame to violate the pledge you made. But O king, none praises you for your this kindly disposition.

verses.sanskrit: श्रोत्रियस्येव ते राजन्मन्दकस्याविपश्चितः। अनुवाकहता बुद्धिर्नैषा तत्त्वार्थदर्शिनी॥१९॥
verses.english: O king, your intellect cannot see the truth like that of a foolish and ignorant man, though of high birth, who has committed to memory the Vedas without understanding them. sons
verses.bhavadeepa: घृणाविष्टः कथं सत्यं त्यजेयमिति लज्जया व्याप्तः आनृशंस्यात् दयालुत्वात् ॥१८॥

verses.sanskrit: घृणी ब्राह्मणरूपोऽसि कथं क्षत्रेषु जायथाः। अस्यां हि योनौ जायन्ते प्रायशः क्रूरबुद्धयः॥२०॥
verses.english: You are kind as a Brahmana; how have you been born in the Kshatriya order? Those born in it (the Kshatriya order) are generally crooked-minded.
verses.bhavadeepa: मन्दकस्य कुत्सितमन्दस्य अनुवाकः गुरूक्तिमनुवचनं तेन हता । अर्थज्ञानशून्यस्य वेदाक्षरमात्राभ्यासिनः ॥१९॥

verses.sanskrit: अश्रौषीस्त्वं राजधर्मान्यथा वै मनुरब्रवीत्। क्रूरान्निकृतिसम्पन्नान्विहितानशमात्मकान्॥२१॥
verses.english: You have heard the duties of kings told by Manu, they are fraught with crookedness and unfairness, they are perfectly opposed to peace and virtue. O great king, why do you then forgive the wicked-minded of Dhritarashtra. O foremost of men, why are you silent in performing your duties being a man of ' high birth?

verses.sanskrit: धार्तराष्ट्रान्महाराज क्षमसे किं दुरात्मनः। कर्तव्ये पुरुषव्याघ्र किमास्से पीठसर्पवत्॥२२॥
बुद्ध्या वीर्येण संयुक्तः श्रुतेनाभिजनेन च। तृणानां मुष्टिनैकेन हिमवन्तं च पर्वतम्॥२३॥
छन्नमिच्छसि कौन्तेय योऽस्मान्संवर्तुमिच्छसि। अशातचर्या गूढेन पृथिव्यां विश्रुतेन च॥२४॥
verses.english: O son of Kunti, who wishes to conceal the Himalayas by means of a handful of grass.

verses.sanskrit: दिवीव पार्थ सूर्येण न शक्याचरितुं त्वया। बृहच्छाल इवानूपे शाखापुष्पपलाशवान्॥२५॥
verses.english: Known as you are all over the world, you will hardly be able to live unknown and undiscovered. O son of Pritha, the sun can never pass through the sky unknown to men.

verses.sanskrit: हस्ती श्वेत इवाज्ञातः कथं जिष्णुश्चरिष्यति। इमौ च सिंहसङ्काशौ भ्रातरौ सहितौ शिशू॥२६॥
verses.english: A large tree with spreading branches; flowers and with leaves in a well watered place (can never remain hidden). Nor can the Airavat (Indra's elephant). How will Jishnu (Arjuna) be able to live undiscovered and unknown?

verses.sanskrit: नकुलः सहदेवश्च कथं पार्थ चरिष्यतः। पुण्यकीर्ती राजपुत्री द्रौपदी वीरसूरियम्॥२७॥
विश्रुता कथमज्ञाता कृष्णा पार्थ चरिष्यति। मां चापि राजञ्जानन्ति ह्याकुमारमिमाः प्रजाः॥२८॥
verses.english: The mother of heroes, the princess Draupadi of virtuous deeds. O son of Pritha, how will this Krishna be able to live undiscovered and unknown?

verses.sanskrit: नाज्ञातचर्यां पश्यामि मेरोरिव निगूहनम्। तथैव बहवोऽस्माभी राष्ट्रभ्यो विप्रवासिताः॥२९॥
verses.english: O king, all the people know me from my childhood. I do not see how I shall be able to live undiscovered and unknown. The Meru (mountains) might as well be concealed!

verses.sanskrit: राजानो राजपुत्राश्च धृतराष्ट्रमनुव्रताः। न हि तेऽप्युपशाम्यन्ति निकृता वा निराकृताः॥३०॥
verses.english: Then again many kings have been driven away from their kingdoms. These kings and princes will all follow the wicked son of Dhritarashtra. For robbed and exiled by us, they cannot be friendly towards us.

verses.sanskrit: अवश्यं तैर्निकर्तव्यमस्माकं तत्प्रियैषिभिः। तेऽप्यस्मासु प्रयुञ्जीरन्प्रच्छन्नान्सुबहूंश्चरान्। आचक्षीरंश्च नो ज्ञात्वा ततः स्यात्सुमहद्भयम्॥३१॥
verses.english: They will certainly seek to injure us with the desire of doing good to him (Duryodhana); and they will certainly set against us many spies in disguise. If they discover us and report it, a great calamity will (then) befall us.

verses.sanskrit: अस्माभिरुषिताः सम्यग्वने मासास्त्रयोदश। परिमाणेन तान्पश्य तावतः परिवत्सरान्॥३२॥
verses.english: We have already lived in the forest for full thirteen months. Consider them for their length as full thirteen years.

verses.sanskrit: अस्ति मासः प्रतिनिधिर्यथा प्राहुर्मनीषिणः। पूतिकानिव सोमस्य तथेदं क्रियतामिति॥३३॥
verses.english: The wise men have said that a month is (but) a substitute for a year, as Pritika is considered as a substitute for the Soma.

verses.sanskrit: अथवाऽनडुहे राजन्साधवे साधुवाहिने। सौहित्यदानादेतस्मादेनसः प्रतिमुच्यते॥३४॥
verses.english: O king, (if you violate the pledge) you may free yourself from its sin by offering good food to a well-conducted bull which carries sacred burdens.

verses.sanskrit: तस्माच्छत्रुवधे राजन्क्रियतां निश्चयस्त्वया। क्षत्रियस्य हि सर्वस्य नान्यो धर्मोऽस्ति संयुगात्॥३५॥
verses.english: O king, therefore make up your mind to kill your enemies. There is no virtue higher to a Kshatriya than battle.
